understood.subject: physics
understood.topic: The principle of inertia (Newton's first law)

lesson.explanationSimple: The principle of inertia says: if no force acts on an object — or if the forces acting on it cancel out (their sum is zero) — then an object at rest stays at rest, and a moving object keeps moving in a straight line at a constant speed. An everyday example: when a bus brakes suddenly, passengers lurch forward, because their bodies were moving and tend to keep moving. That is why seat belts matter.
lesson.explanationFormal: Principle of inertia (Newton's first law): in a Galilean reference frame, if a body is pseudo-isolated (the vector sum of the forces acting on it is zero), its centre of inertia is either at rest or in uniform rectilinear motion. Conversely, if the centre of inertia of a body is at rest or in uniform rectilinear motion, the vector sum of the forces acting on it is zero.
steps: Identify the forces acting on the object.
Check whether the forces cancel out (their sum is zero).
If the sum is zero: the object is either at rest or moving in a straight line at constant speed.
If the motion changes (speed or direction), the sum of the forces is not zero.

example.problem: A book lies on a table and does not move. Are there forces acting on it?
example.solution: Yes: its weight (the Earth pulls the book down) and the reaction of the table (pushing the book up). These two forces have the same strength and opposite directions, so their sum is zero — which is why the book stays at rest, as the principle of inertia says.

exercises.prompt: An object moves in a straight line at a constant speed. What can we say about the forces acting on it?
exercises.hint: Go back to the principle: what happens when the sum of the forces is zero?
exercises.explanation: By the principle of inertia, uniform straight-line motion means the forces cancel out (their vector sum is zero). It does not necessarily mean that no force acts.

choices.text: No force at all must be acting on it
The forces cancel out (their sum is zero)
A large force is pushing it forward

exercises.prompt: Why do passengers lurch forward when a bus brakes suddenly?
exercises.hint: The passenger's body was moving before the braking.
exercises.explanation: The passenger's body tends to keep moving (inertia) while the bus stops, so the passenger appears to be pushed forward.

choices.text: Because their bodies tend to keep moving
Because the bus pushes them forward
Because wind comes in through the windows

exercises.prompt: In your own words, explain the principle of inertia.
exercises.hint: Talk about the forces, and about two cases: an object at rest and a moving object.
exercises.explanation: If the forces acting on an object cancel out, the object either stays at rest or keeps moving in a straight line at constant speed.

criteria.description: Mentions the condition: no net force / forces cancel out (sum of forces is zero)
States the result: the body stays at rest or keeps moving in a straight line at constant speed

acceptedExamples: If the forces cancel out, the object stays at rest or keeps moving at the same speed in a straight line
When the net force on an object is zero, it either stays still or keeps moving in a straight line at the same speed

misconceptions.description: Believes a constant force is needed to keep a body moving at constant speed

exercises.modelAnswer: If the sum of the forces acting on an object is zero (the forces cancel out), an object at rest stays at rest, and a moving object keeps moving in a straight line at constant speed.
